paper.title: Optimal Design for Reward Modeling in RLHF

settings.name_in_paper: Offline linear contextual dueling bandit (simple regret) for RLHF dataset selection
unmapped: Bradley-Terry / logistic preference feedback Y_t ~ Ber(sigma(<theta*, a_t - a'_t>)) on pairs from the same prompt set A_n
Fully offline (non-adaptive) design: all T pairs chosen before any feedback is observed
Simple regret is the max over N given action sets A_n of the gap of the recommended action
Action sets (A_n) arbitrary (worst case), theta* in unit ball
settings.definition_quote: \regret_{\alg}(T, (\cA_n)_{n \in [N]}, \theta^\star) = \max_{n \in [N]}\max_{a \in \cA_n} \ps{\theta^\star}{a- \hat{a}_T(\cA_n)} ... For any $x,y \in \cX \times \cY, \psi(x,y) \in \oball(0,1)$ ... We also suppose that $\theta^\star \in \oball(0,1)$.

settings.name_in_paper: Changing action set (online) dueling setting (lower bound)
unmapped: At each step t an action set A_t is given and a pair from A_t^2 is chosen; logistic preference feedback; simple regret is max over all A_t of gap of predicted best action
settings.definition_quote: at each step $t \in [T]$, an action set $\cA_t, t \in [T]$ is provided and the algorithm must select a pair of samples $(\al_t, \am_t) \in \cA_t^2$.

symbols.eps_alg: approximation parameter: hat{pi} is a (1+epsilon)-approximation of the optimal design

conditions: actions and theta* in the unit ball (H1)
tuning: samples drawn according to a (1+epsilon)-approximate optimal design

source.label: theorem:simple_regret_upper_bound
source.quote: Let $\epsilon >0$ and suppose that we collect at least $T\geq d^2$ samples according to an $(1+\epsilon)$ approximation $\hat{\pi}$ of the optimal design policy $\pi^\star$ for the problem. Then, for any $\cB$ and $\theta^\star \in \oball(0,1)$, with probability at least $1-\delta$, ... $\regret(T, (\cA_n)_{n \in [N]}, \theta^\star) \leq 20 (1+\epsilon)\, \sqrt{d/T} \times [\sqrt{2 \log (1/\delta) + d\, \log(\lambda^{1-1/d}+4T/d\lambda^{1/d} )} + \sqrt{\lambda} ]$.

results.notes: Interpreted 4T/d\lambda^{1/d} as 4T/(d lambda^{1/d}) per the proof. Regret here is the realized simple regret holding w.p. 1-delta.

conditions: actions and theta* in the unit ball (H1)
tuning: hat{pi} is a 3/2-approximation of the optimal design

source.label: corollary:simple_regret_upper_bound
source.quote: Suppose that we have selected the samples $\dselect$ to label under $\hat{\pi}$, a $3/2$-approximation of the optimal design policy $\pi^\star$. Choosing $\lambda = 1/d$ for the regularization, for any $\delta \in (0,1)$, under the conditions of Theorem, with probability at least $1-\delta$, we have that $\regret \leq 30\sqrt{d/T} \times [\sqrt{2 \log(1/\delta) + d\log((1+4T)/d^{1-1/d})}+1/\sqrt{d} ]$

conditions: actions and theta* in the unit ball (H1)
tuning: hat{pi} is a 3/2-approximation of the optimal design

source.label: corollary:simple_regret_upper_bound
source.quote: and as a consequence, choosing $\delta = d^{1-1/d}/(4T+1)$, we can bound the expectation of the regret as $\E[\regret(T, (\cA_n)_{n \in [N]}, \theta^\star)] \leq 30 \frac{d+2}{\sqrt{T}}\sqrt{\log(\frac{4T+1}{d^{1-1/d}})} + 31/\sqrt{T}$.

results.notes: Expected simple regret, second part of the corollary.

conditions: hard instance: action set [-1/sqrt(d), 1/sqrt(d)]^d, theta in {±sqrt(d/T)}^d

source.label: theorem:lower_bound
source.quote: Suppose that $d \geq 16$ and that $T \geq d^2$. For any algorithm $\alg$ which samples $T$ pairs from $\cB$ and receives a preference feedback before outputing an action $\hat{a}(\cA_n) \in \cA_n$ for an input $\cA_n$, there exists $(\cA_n)_{n \in [N]} \subseteq \oball(0,1)$ as well as $\theta^\star \in \oball(0,1)$ such that $\regret(T, (\cA_n)_{n \in [N]}, \theta^\star) \geq d \, \rme^{-5}/4\sqrt{T}$.

results.notes: Statement does not specify expectation, but the proof lower-bounds the expected regret under P_theta*; recorded as expectation. Read as d e^{-5}/(4 sqrt(T)) per the proof.

symbols.c_const: some constant c > 0 independent of T and d

conditions: adversarially chosen action sets: A_1..A_{T-1} = {±e_1}, A_T = {±e_2}, theta* in {±e_2}

source.label: lemma:lower_bound_online
source.quote: Consider the $2$-dimensional euclidian space Span$(e_1, e_2)$ as the whole action space. In that case, there exists a set of actions $(\cA_t)_{t \in [T]}$ and some $\theta^\star \in \oball(0,1)$ such the regret defined in \eqref{equation:definition_online_regret} for any algorithm $\alg$ satisfies $\regret_\alg(T, (\cA_t)_{t \in [T]}, \theta^\star) \geq \rme^{-c}/2$, for some $c >0$ independent of $T$ and $d$.

results.notes: Constant (non-vanishing) simple regret with changing adversarial action sets; probabilistic type not stated explicitly, proof is in-expectation style via Bretagnolle-Huber.
